subject: Private offer for Evergreen Retail — commission & discount exception
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@amazon.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Evergreen Retail private offer - commission carveout

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the run-through this morning. Evergreen (Marta) is ready to move quickly but needs a private offer in the AWS marketplace to include a one-time onboarding discount and a modified rev-share profile to support co-marketing. To be concrete: AWS is requesting a 20% marketplace rev-share for the first 12 months and Evergreen is asking for a 30% list-price discount for year one.

Standard Redwood marketplace terms don't allow a >25% discount without exec review and rev-share requests like this require Deal Desk sign-off. I've attached a draft private offer and a quick commission calc for AWS to show the economics. Can you confirm Redwood can accept the 20% rev-share + 30% discount as-is, or what counter you'd like?

Attachments: Evergreen_Private_Offer_Draft.pdf, AWS_Commission_Calc.xlsx

Appreciate a fast turnaround — Evergreen is targeting a commitment by EOD Thursday PT.

Sanjay Rao
Senior Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
Amazon Web Services
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: Evergreen Retail private offer - commission carveout

Team — forwarding AWS's ask. Quick summary: 20% AWS rev-share for 12 months + Evergreen wants 30% off list for year one. Deal: ~ $480k ARR initial commit if signed.

Immediate asks:
- Finance (Marissa) — can we absorb 30% one-off (or cap at 25%)? Please provide modeled ARR and P&L impact.
- Partnerships (Vivek) — signal whether this is strategic enough to accept the proposed split.
- Legal (Jonas) — initial redlines for any marketplace-private-offer language, IP/data handling, and rev-share mechanics so we can present a single document to AWS and Evergreen.

I've attached the draft and AWS calc. I recommend we push back to 25% discount / 15% rev-share unless we get marketing co-funding from AWS. Need exec sign-off if we stay at 30%/20%.

Thanks — k

--
Kimberly Park
Director, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Evergreen Retail private offer - commission carveout

Kimberly —

I ran rough numbers on the attachments. If we accept 30% discount + the AWS 20% take, contribution margin for year one turns negative on this ARR band without offset. Two comments:

1) We can consider a step-down approach: 30% discount only on first 3 months (or onboarding credit) with billback to full price after month 4, or 25% flat for year one.
2) Any discount >25% requires CRO approval per commercial policy; rev-share >15% also needs finance + partnerships to sign off.

Please provide an ARR phasing (monthly expected consumption) and any marketing credits AWS is offering. With that I'll model cashflow and impact to FY27 bookings. Without a material marketing subsidy or higher net-new ARR commitment, I recommend we do not accept 30% list discount.

Marissa
Head of Finance, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Evergreen Retail private offer - commission carveout

FYI — I spoke with Sanjay and Evergreen separately. Strategic context: Evergreen is a marquee retail brand (national roll-out) and AWS has offered a co-marketing commitment (digital placement + a $50k MDF) contingent on the 20% rev-share. If we can secure at least $40k of marketing funds (AWS + Evergreen), the CAC delta is mitigated and we get high-visibility proof point in Q3.

Proposed Redwood counter (balanced):
- 20% rev-share to AWS for first 12 months (as requested)
- 20% list-price discount to Evergreen for first 12 months (not 30%)
- Marketing fund requirement: AWS/Evergreen to commit $40k combined; Redwood will commit an additional $15k of co-op credits tied to deliverables.
- 12-month pilot, auto-review at month 10 with performance KPIs (MAU, activation, retention).

If finance/legal can sign off on the pilot language and indemnities, I recommend we escalate to execs for margin exception approval on the 20% rev-share if the above marketing funding is documented.

— Vivek
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Evergreen Retail private offer - commission carveout

Team — attached are legal redlines to the Evergreen draft (Evergreen_Private_Offer_Redline.pdf). Major asks:
- Clarify rev-share payment cadence and audit rights; we need the ability to audit AWS-collected payments tied to this offer.
- Add explicit data-handling clause: Redwood's customer data cannot be used by AWS for unrelated advertising; include a 90-day data deletion window after contract termination for any exported logs.
- Indemnity carveouts: no open-ended liability for Redwood for AWS marketplace distribution.

Also, do not execute DocuSign until we confirm AWS's contract team accepts our redlines. I will reach out to AWS counsel, but want Deal Desk to confirm the financial sheet we will present.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: REQUEST: Executive sign-off needed — Evergreen private offer (time-sensitive)

Aditya —

Requesting a rapid executive sign-off on a one-off margin exception for a marketplace private offer with Evergreen Retail (details below). This is an escalation per policy because the proposed economics exceed standard discount/rev-share thresholds.

Deal snapshot (concise):
- Customer: Evergreen Retail (national retail rollout)
- Proposed Redwood list discount: 20% (counter; AWS/Customer asked for 30%)
- AWS Marketplace rev-share request: 20% for first 12 months (AWS ask; we propose honoring given marketing funding conditions)
- Term: 12-month pilot, auto-review at month 10 with KPIs
- Estimated first-year ARR: $480,000
- Marketing funds: AWS + Evergreen to commit combined >= $40k; Redwood will contribute $15k of co-op credits if KPIs met
- Outstanding items: legal redlines (attached), exact revenue phasing (Marissa), and AWS counsel acceptance of redlines

Decision requested: please approve one of the following by EOD Thursday PT so we can proceed with AWS/Evergreen:
1) APPROVE the counter (20% discount / AWS 20% rev-share) subject to marketing fund commitments and legal redlines; OR
2) REQUEST CRO-level review to allow 25–30% discount or higher rev-share; OR
3) DECLINE — ask Kimber/partnerships to rework economics (preferred fallback: 25% discount / 15% rev-share).

Link to HubSpot deal and DocuSign preview: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567 | https://www.docusign.net/sign/ABCDEF

Thanks — please reply with option 1/2/3 or any modifications.

Kimberly Park
Director, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
